Use `snl info` to discover the workspace version, capabilities, and current configuration before choosing another command.

### Command path
`info` is the canonical transport-neutral command. The shell adapter is `snl info`; an Agent/MCP adapter submits the same operation object instead of reconstructing shell text.

### Operation request
```json
{"protocol":"snl.operation/v1","command":"info","root":"/absolute/workspace","arguments":{}}
```
Every adapter accepts exactly this semantic request. Unknown argument keys are rejected. The CLI accepts `--root` and `--json` globally and emits one complete JSON document followed by a newline. Corrupt or unsupported workspaces fail closed instead of returning partial capabilities.

### Success result
A successful call exits `0` and returns `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":true,"command":"info","data":...,"diagnostics":[]}`. `data` contains canonical root, schema/topology versions, entity counts, capabilities, and the available command registry version.

### Failure and exit semantics
Domain rejection (invalid data, not-found, conflict, or validation errors) exits `1`. Invocation, input I/O, unsupported workspace/schema, lock acquisition, and runtime failures exit `2`. Failure stdout under `--json` is exactly one `{"protocol":"snl.result/v1","ok":false,"command":"info","error":{"code":"<stable-code>","message":"<actionable text>","details":...,"retryable":false}}`; no stack trace or prose contaminates stdout.

### State and concurrency
Read-only and stateless. Revisions, cursors, checked digests, and workspace revisions are opaque tokens. Repeated calls against unchanged bytes return equivalent semantic results.
